data.hypothesis: Retaining the measured warp-shuffle kernel while replacing per-interaction sqrt/division with a refined reciprocal-square-root inverse-cube calculation may reduce arithmetic cost. The transformation is unmeasured in combination and must pass all correctness and performance checks.

memory_lessons.applicability: The rsqrt-based calculation has been checked as a standalone candidate, but was slower than the best warp-shuffle candidate; combining these different kernels may behave differently and needs a fresh measurement.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured warp-shuffle candidate was correct and faster than baseline, while the separately measured refined-rsqrt candidate was correct but slower than the warp-shuffle candidate.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this combined kernel against the warp-shuffle base on all official sizes and correctness cases.

data.notes: Only src/nbody_kernel.cu changes; launch.json remains unchanged. This is a proposal, not a correctness result or confirmed speedup.
transformations: Retain warp-level source broadcast, complete-tile and tail handling, and target validity guards from the measured base.
Use rsqrtf with two Newton refinements to form the inverse distance cubed in both interaction paths, replacing sqrtf and division.
Preserve the target-mass force accumulation, self-interaction exclusion, integration order, particle layout, and launch configuration.
